dossier_meta.statement_text: For any fixed integer $c \geq 2$, there exists an integer $t$ such that for infinitely many graphs $H$ with treewidth $t$ and paths $P$, every $c$-colouring of $H \boxtimes P$ has clustering $\Omega(|V(H \boxtimes P)|^{c/(c^2-c+1)})$.
dossier_meta.context_text: The upper bound in Theorem 4 gives that $H_1 \boxtimes H_2$ is $c$-colourable with clustering $O(|V(H_1 \boxtimes H_2)|^{c/(c^2-c+1)})$ when one graph has bounded degree. The authors believe this upper bound is asymptotically tight, and furthermore conjecture that there exists a matching construction where the bounded-degree graph is a path.
